answer: Trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on an attestation graph, with voting weight derived from visitation probability starting at trusted seeds. A sybil cluster may be internally dense but separated by a sparse external cut; low conductance limits walk flow across that boundary. Given seed-normalized scoring and bounded cut capacity, min-cut transitivity bounds the cluster’s aggregate vote by the trusted mass that can reach it, even if its nodes are named relic, meadow, and basalt.
